category_title: Blind student with selective mutism and high receptive language skills
minimal_context: Sally is using a voice-output device to answer listening comprehension questions after reading a story in Braille.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We just finished the story. Now I am going to ask you a comprehension question.

STUDENT: (Sally finishes tactually tracking the Braille lines with the fingertips of both hands.)

TUTOR: Here is the voice-output device. Did the main character go to the store? Press yes or no.

STUDENT: (Sally independently places her hand on the communicator.)

TUTOR: What is your answer? Go ahead and press a button.

STUDENT: (Sally hesitates after placing her hand on the communicator, remaining silent and not pressing a response.)

options.A: Fade out the M&M reinforcers while continuing verbal praise that is specific for good reading.
options.B: Provide access to more socially appropriate sensory stimulation by giving her a squishy stress ball.
options.C: Ensure that most lessons throughout the intervention follow the exact same sequence of tasks.
options.D: Incorporate her preferred story topics into the comprehension questions during the intervention.
